question: Which class resides at the root of the entire class inheritance hierarchy in Java?

options.text: Object
None, classes without an extends clause have no superclass
Class
System

explanation: In Java, java.lang.Object is the single root of the entire class hierarchy. Any class that does not explicitly specify an extends clause automatically inherits directly from Object.

question: Can two sibling classes that both directly extend the same superclass be assigned to each other's reference variables?

options.text: Yes, sibling classes are interchangeable because they share the same parent class.
Yes, provided neither class declares an explicit constructor.
Yes, but only if explicit downcasting is applied without an instanceof check.
No, sibling classes have incompatible types and assignment causes a compile error.

explanation: Sibling classes share a common ancestor but have distinct, incompatible types. A reference of one sibling cannot hold an instance of another sibling, resulting in a compile-time incompatible types error.

question: What happens during subclass instantiation if the subclass constructor does not contain an explicit super() call?

options.text: The compiler automatically inserts an implicit super() call to run the parent no-arg constructor.
The superclass constructor is completely skipped and its fields remain uninitialized.
The subclass object bypasses the Object class hierarchy entirely.
The JVM throws a ClassCastException at runtime during memory allocation.

explanation: If a constructor body does not start with an explicit this(...) or super(...) call, the Java compiler automatically inserts super() to guarantee that the parent class constructor executes first.

question: What danger exists when performing an explicit downcast from a superclass reference to a subclass type?

options.text: None, downcasting is always guaranteed safe by the compiler if the code compiles cleanly.
It throws a ClassCastException at runtime if the referenced object is not an instance of the target subclass.
It causes the parent constructor to re-execute and wipe the object state.
It disconnects the object from the Object root hierarchy.

explanation: Downcasting instructs the compiler to treat a supertype reference as a subtype. If the actual object on the heap at runtime does not belong to that subtype, the JVM throws a ClassCastException.
